periods.analysis: The Summer Learning Access Initiative is green at 9% complete, establishing the baseline for this multi-quarter build. The important resident-facing foundation is in place: site selection for the 6 neighborhood locations is complete, giving families predictable access points across East Harbor, Bayside, Northgate, South Pier, Westview, and the Airport Corridor. Instructor hiring and training is in-progress, while enrollment opens and summer session launch have not started, which is appropriate at this early stage. From a resident outcome lens, we are turning empty summer weeks into structured learning time before chronic absenteeism can harden into a school-year pattern.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the green trajectory by locking site operating agreements and room schedules for all 6 locations before programming details expand. Extend the instructor pipeline through library youth-services staff, recreation aides, and vetted Harborview State education majors so training can move without narrowing access. Prepare the enrollment playbook now, including multilingual family notices and referral lists from school attendance teams, even though enrollment has not started.

periods.analysis: The initiative remains green at 12% complete, up 3 percentage points from 9% in 2024-Q3. Site selection for the 6 neighborhood locations remains complete, and the team used the quarter well to translate those locations into operating plans for classrooms, gym time, library computer labs, and safe arrival routes. Instructor hiring and training remains in-progress, with priority placed on staff who can support reading recovery, STEM enrichment, and trauma-informed youth engagement. Enrollment opens and summer session launch remain not-started, but the work is moving in the right order: first make the promise reliable, then invite families into it.
periods.recommendations: Sustain progress by completing walk-through checklists at each site with Facilities, Library branch managers, and Recreation supervisors. Extend the training model with a standard two-hour module on attendance nudges, family contact protocols, and mandated reporting so every instructor carries the same expectations. Keep a watch list of sites needing shade, Wi-Fi, or custodial coverage before enrollment materials are released.

periods.recommendations: Sustain the green status by finalizing the site-by-site capacity model, including maximum daily attendance, meal service space, and severe-weather indoor plans. Extend outreach preparation by giving school counselors and family liaisons a draft referral script for students with spring attendance concerns. Require weekly recruiting reports that separate certified teachers, college tutors, recreation aides, and substitute instructors so we can see any staffing gap early.

Extend training with a tabletop exercise for heat advisories, tidal flooding detours near South Pier, and same-day instructor absences. Prepare enrollment materials in English, Spanish, Vietnamese, and Arabic so the city is ready to move quickly when that milestone starts.

Extend the staff-development plan with short observed practice sessions using the actual reading, math, and enrichment materials planned for summer. Build a family-support checklist now that includes transportation barriers, device access, meal needs, and attendance risk flags before enrollment begins.

periods.recommendations: Sustain progress by converting the 6 site plans into purchase lists for books, STEM kits, recreation supplies, first-aid materials, and wayfinding signs. periods.analysis: The initiative is green at 27% complete, up 3 percentage points from 24% in 2025-Q4. periods.recommendations: Sustain the green trajectory by running readiness reviews at each site with Parks, Libraries, Facilities, IT, and the school district liaison in the same room. Extend the training work with a final skills inventory that identifies which instructors can lead literacy intervention, STEM labs, adaptive recreation, and bilingual family communication. Pre-load the enrollment system fields and referral codes now so families are not slowed down once enrollment opens.

periods.analysis: The initiative remains green at 30% complete, up 3 percentage points from 27% in 2026-Q1. Across the eight-quarter arc, the work has moved steadily from a 9% baseline to 30% complete without losing the fundamentals: site selection for the 6 neighborhood locations is complete, and instructor hiring and training remains in-progress. Enrollment opens and summer session launch are still not-started, which is the clearest next threshold for turning strong preparation into direct family access. The result is healthy and forward-looking, but the resident promise now depends on moving from readiness to activation with the same care.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the green status by completing a go/no-go checklist for each of the 6 sites covering staffing, supplies, technology, safety, meals, and family communications. Extend the initiative by scheduling enrollment-opening rehearsals with call-center staff, branch librarians, and recreation front desks so residents get consistent answers. Set the next-quarter action target around launching enrollment only after instructor coverage and site readiness are verified, then use waitlist data to decide whether to add pop-up seats at libraries or community centers.
